title: Crash-safe Print Queue mixed-batch recovery and provider outcome fencing

acceptanceCriteria.description: Recovery plans from durable per-order sidecars, continues unrelated safe orders after a mixed-batch interruption, and never resends provider-pending orders even when the parent result snapshot is stale.

Ambiguous ShipStation operations are reconciled only by exact normalized external_shipment_id reads; verified receipts resume the existing atomic persistence owner, while absent effects require cancellation acknowledgement plus a consistency grace and no provider POST is issued.

Automatic pg-boss postage-chunk redelivery is disabled, durable recovery is the sole replay owner, and active locks, held operations, missing post-purchase artifacts, and unresolved legacy intents remain non-retryable reconciliation states.

Selected-rate proof storage fails closed on cache/database unavailability, scheduled pre-expiry refresh persists purchase-valid account authorization and selectionRef, and cross-order, cross-account, and shipment-fact mismatches reject before the provider.

The Orders UI renders backend-owned per-order outcomes and next actions, retains interrupted jobs across reload, and sends only an opaque job id with an empty body when an operator resumes safe items.

Carrier outage, insufficient balance, rate-authority outage, stale proof, and provider ambiguity produce distinct backend next actions; only true rate-proof failures request rerating and provider ambiguity is never retry-eligible.

The focused Print Queue, provider-ledger, mixed-success, durable recovery, rate-authority, label URL, invalid-label, strict TypeScript, production frontend build, browser, and all 49 mandatory source-of-truth gates pass at the reviewed SHA.

Shipped/cancelled edit locks, schemas, inventory deduction kill switch, and read-only UI protections were not weakened; verification bought no postage, called no live carrier mutation, notified no marketplace, and performed no production order, shipment, billing, or inventory mutation.

sotBypass.details: Durable backend sidecars and the provider-operation ledger remain authoritative. Routes and UI transport/render their facts, and the provider adapter only normalizes provider payloads.

evidence.proves: A 32-order mixed fixture resumes 20 independently safe items while fencing three ambiguous provider outcomes, then reports 29 queued and three reconciliation-required outcomes with no retry eligibility.

The real Orders UI renders interrupted per-order outcomes, posts an empty resume body to the job-id route, hides resume when only provider ambiguity remains, and never starts PDF printing or a label request. Every network request is mocked.
A fake-provider migrated-database integration turns ambiguous post-dispatch failure into a durable hold, blocks redispatch, records an exact receipt, and consumes the local effect once.
The migrated worker fixture admits one current recovery generation, rejects stale writes and old claims, and distinguishes infrastructure restart from provider reconciliation holds.

evidence.proves: Injected stale claims, timeout/skew faults, ambiguous provider acceptance, local receipt loss, and overlapping recovery generations fail closed and cannot cause a second provider effect.
Backend-issued quote authorization rejects cross-order, cross-account, and shipment-fact drift before the injected provider spy, while one valid exact proof reaches it once.

evidence.proves: The release restores the last production-compatible inventory runtime after PS-439's read-only discrepancy gate blocked cutover, preserves the INVENTORY_AUTO_DEDUCT kill switch and PS-424 fulfillment-facts boundary, and requires only the already-live schema through 0072. Against the last proven production SHA, the target contains PS-444 durable queue recovery plus a required override comment in the restored kill-switch-protected inventory deduction path. It contains no migration, orders/shipments schema change, order edit route change, marketplace notification change, or production data script; shipping-sensitive changes remain bounded to durable queue recovery, receipt validation, and thin outcome rendering.

migrations.rollbackPlan: No schema or data rollback is required. PS-439 migration 0073 was never applied in production and is absent from this target, which retains runtime readiness through 0072. If PS-444 must roll back, deploy the prior proven SHA and preserve all durable queue, provider receipt, shipment, and order history.

rollback.strategy: Forward-revert only the PS-444 implementation and packet, or redeploy frontend, API, and workers at prior proven SHA 6a9faa1aa59f78c123fe27064a867913b3ade783. Do not restore the blocked PS-439 cutover. Never delete provider receipts, replay provider-pending work, or rewrite shipped/cancelled history during rollback.

liveVerification.reason: Behavioral closure is intentionally offline because a live label/queue mutation could buy postage or alter production order and shipment state. Production deployment is verified separately with credential-free health/readiness and commit-parity checks only.
